title: Antipsychotic-related brain changes in first-episode psychosis: A systematic review
title_zh: 首发精神病相关的抗精神病药物脑变化：系统评价
abstract: BACKGROUND: Antipsychotics (APs) induce functional, anatomical, and metabolic brain changes in schizophrenia, but the nature and clinical significance of these effects remain debated. Focusing on first-episode psychosis (FEP) allows distinction between medication-induced and illness-related brain changes and facilitates identification of early predictors of treatment response. DESIGN: Following PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO: CRD42021240369), we systematically reviewed longitudinal neuroimaging studies in FEP with the objective of 1) identifying APs-induced brain changes, 2) identifying brain changes associated with clinical improvement, and 3) exploring the potential of neuroimaging biomarkers to predict treatment response. RESULTS: Eighty-six studies were included: 26 structural, 27 functional, and 16 metabolic, including 33 studies specifically addressing predictive biomarkers of treatment response. Across modalities, APs induced measurable brain changes within days to weeks of treatment Ainitiation, particularly in the striatum, thalamus, and prefrontal cortex (PFC), key regions of the striato-thalamo-cortical network. Increased basal ganglia gray matter volume was the most consistent anatomical finding; cortical findings, particularly in the PFC, were more heterogeneous, with both increases and decreases in thickness reported across studies. Functionally, APs normalized abnormal striatal activity and connectivity, correlating with improvement in positive symptoms. In contrast, no reliable imaging correlate has been identified for changes in negative or cognitive symptoms. Metabolic studies showed increased N-acetylaspartate in the thalamus and PFC and normalization of glutamate levels in associative and limbic regions. Baseline brain characteristics, particularly less severe structural or functional abnormalities in the striatum and anterior cingulate cortex, predicted better outcomes. CONCLUSION: Together, these findings suggest that APs primarily act through modulation and normalization of striato-cortical circuits, with preserved neuroplasticity favoring recovery. Integrating multimodal neuroimaging and computational approaches may advance biomarker-based, individualized treatment strategies in early psychosis.
abstract_zh: 背景：抗精神病药物（AP）在精神分裂症患者中诱导功能、解剖和代谢脑变化，但这些效应的性质和临床意义仍存在争议。聚焦于首发精神病（FEP）允许在药物效应和疾病相关脑变化之间进行区分，并有助于识别早期治疗响应预测因子。设计：遵循PRISMA指南（PROSPERO：CRD42021240369），我们系统回顾了首发精神病患者的纵向脑成像研究，旨在1）识别抗精神病药物诱导的脑变化，2）识别与临床改善相关的脑变化，3）探索预测治疗响应的神经影像生物标志物的潜力。结果：共纳入86项研究：26项结构研究、27项功能研究和16项代谢研究，其中33项专门研究治疗响应的预测生物标志物。跨模态，抗精神病药物在治疗开始后几天至几周内诱导可测量的脑变化，特别是在纹状体、丘脑和前额叶皮层（PFC）中，这些是纹状-丘脑-皮层网络的关键区域。基底神经节灰质体积增加是最一致的解剖学发现；特别是在前额叶皮层方面的皮层发现异质性较大，不同研究报道了皮层厚度的增加和减少。功能上，抗精神病药物正常化了异常的纹状体活动和连接性，这与积极症状改善相关。相反，尚未识别出负性症状或认知症状变化的可靠成像相关物。代谢研究显示，丘脑和前额叶N-乙酰天冬氨酸增加，以及联合和边缘区域谷氨酸水平的正常化。基线脑特征，特别是纹状体和前扣带回结构或功能异常程度较轻，预测了更好的预后。结论：这些发现共同表明，抗精神病药物主要通过调节和正常化纹状-皮层电路发挥作用，保留的神经可塑性有利于恢复。整合多模态神经影像和计算方法可能有助于推进早期精神病个体化治疗的生物标志物导向策略。
